hotspots.title: Nairobi–Mombasa highway, Makueni stretch
hotspots.summary: The Salama pilgrims’ crash on 3 October, a second pile-up at Salama the next day, and the Mtito Andei bus–lorry collision on 25 October. The two worst crashes of the year happened 70 km apart on the same road, and together killed 39 people.

hotspots.title: Nakuru–Eldoret highway
hotspots.summary: The Sachangwan tanker explosion that closed the road on 6 October, a crash that injured 17 mourners, a multi-vehicle crash at Salgaa, and six deaths in a truck–matatu–car collision on the last day of the month.

hotspots.title: Gold mines and quarries
hotspots.summary: Five collapses in West Pokot, Migori and Meru killed 12 people, all in small-scale gold mining or quarrying. Two West Pokot collapses four days apart account for nine of the deaths.

hotspots.title: Northern frontier
hotspots.summary: An al-Shabaab bomb on the Dadaab road, bandit raids in Turkana, Marsabit, Samburu and Isiolo, Ethiopian fighting spilling into Moyale, and two children killed by old ordnance in Garissa. Police officers and reservists were among the dead.

hotspots.title: Homa Bay
hotspots.summary: A police operation against town gangs, which made dozens of arrests and set off protests when an alleged gang leader was held, along with fatal clashes and drownings among Lake Victoria fishermen.

hotspots.title: Kirinyaga
hotspots.summary: A pregnant woman who died after allegedly being pushed from a police car, a petrol attendant set alight, the Kagio market fire, a hippo attack, and two missing men later found dead in a river and a dung pit. A university student missing at Thiba Falls had not been found by month’s end.

watch.title: Short rains and El Niño
watch.body: Tana River floods displaced 302 households in the last days of October, and rain has already flooded Parklands and Mombasa. A girl was swept away in Kajiado and a toddler drowned in a pit in Taveta. Rising Lake Nakuru has displaced 200 families.
watch.action: If you live near the Tana, a river or a drainage channel, know your nearest high ground now. Check the Deckwatch map and Kenya Meteorological Department alerts before travelling in heavy rain, and never cross flowing water.

watch.title: Ebola
watch.body: Kenya had eight confirmed cases and one death by 19 October, all linked to a patient treated in DR Congo. The Health Ministry reports 97% contact tracing and has declared the Bundibugyo strain a formidable epidemic disease. Leaders in western Kenya are warning about cross-border movement.
watch.action: Follow Ministry of Health guidance only. Anyone with fever and bleeding after contact with a sick traveller should call the Ministry of Health hotline before going to a crowded facility.

watch.title: The Mombasa road through Makueni
watch.body: The Salama and Mtito Andei crashes killed 39 people in three weeks. NTSA blamed improper overtaking and driver fatigue on long return trips. Enforcement operations started after Salama.
watch.action: Avoid night travel on the Nairobi–Mombasa highway where you can, and refuse to board a bus whose driver has just completed the outbound trip. Report dangerous PSV driving to NTSA.

watch.title: Building safety after Eastleigh
watch.body: The Eastleigh rescue was still running when the month ended, and a CBD building collapsed during demolition the week before. The DPP says City Hall never filed an inquiry. Residents in Katani have already protested against a storey building.
watch.action: Do not rent in or work on a building under construction without visible approval notices. Report cracks or building work going up too fast to the county’s building inspectorate.

watch.title: Fuel prices and protests
watch.body: EPRA’s fuel price rise brought protests to Nairobi’s CBD and a journalist’s arrest. Matatu operators have raised fares, and activists have announced a march on State House.
watch.action: Check Deckwatch before travelling into the CBD on announced protest days, and plan a route out.

watch.title: The north and the Ethiopian border
watch.body: Raiders struck Kibish, Loiyangalani and Marsabit villages in the last week of October, and fighting in Ethiopia sent hundreds of people across the border at Moyale.
watch.action: Travel in Turkana North, Marsabit and Moyale only with current local information. Keep to daylight and to convoys where they run.

headlines.month: Two bus disasters on the Mombasa road, and Kenya’s first Ebola death
headlines.what: Crime and security made up over four in ten incidents and caused the most deaths. Road crashes killed 68 people, 39 of them in two crashes in Makueni.
